This script integrates taxonomy, genus-level phylogeny, body mass, and
functional group information for species with observed chemical sensitivity
data. Specifically, it:

- builds genus-level phylogenies using the Open Tree of Life;
- matches species to body mass estimates, using genus-level averages when
  species-level data are unavailable;
- assigns ecological functional groups, including resource groups for algae,
  functional feeding groups for invertebrates, and trophic guilds for fish.

The final outputs are taxon-specific datasets and genus-level phylogenies for
algae, invertebrates, and fish.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rm(list=ls())

library(here)
library(tidyverse)  
library(stringr)
library(rotl)
library(ape)
library(ggtree)
library(ggtreeExtra)
library(ggnewscale)
library(data.table)
library(forcats)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)
```

# 1. Load dataset

The observed sensitivity dataset was compiled in
`1_compile_observed_sensitivity_data.Rmd`. Here, we extract unique species and standardise scientific names before matching them to phylogeny, body mass, and functional group information.

```{r}
combined_observed_sensitivity <- readRDS(here("data/1_observed_sensitivity/combined_observed_sensitivity/combined_observed_sensitivity.rds"))

spe_tax_uni <- combined_observed_sensitivity %>%
  select(latin, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus) %>%
  mutate(
    latin = tolower(latin),
    genus = tolower(genus)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(latin)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(genus)) %>%  distinct()

nrow(spe_tax_uni)
n_distinct(spe_tax_uni$latin)
n_distinct(spe_tax_uni$genus)
```

## 1.1 Standardise species names
```{r}
clean_latin_name <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    str_to_lower() %>%
    str_replace_all("\\(.*?\\)", " ") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\[.*?\\]", " ") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\b(cf|aff|sp|spp)\\.?\\b", " ") %>%
    str_replace_all("\\b(var|subsp|ssp|forma|f)\\.?\\b", " ") %>%
    str_squish() %>%
    str_replace("^([a-z]+)\\s+([a-z-]+).*$", "\\1 \\2")
}

spe_tax_clean <- spe_tax_uni %>%
  mutate(
    latin_raw = latin,
    latin = clean_latin_name(latin),
    genus = str_extract(latin, "^[a-z]+")
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(latin), latin != "",
         !is.na(genus), genus != "")

# Manual corrections after screening
spe_tax_clean <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  mutate(
    latin = case_when(
      latin == "lithodes antarcticus" ~ "lithodes antarctica",
      latin == "viviparus bengalensis" ~ "filopaludina bengalensis",
      latin == "acanthomysis sculpta" ~ "holmesimysis sculpta",
      latin == "acartia clausi" ~ "acartia clausii",
      latin == "acartia lillgeborgi" ~ "acartia lilljeborgii",
      latin == "acheilognathus moriokae" ~ "acheilognathus melanogaster",
      latin == "achnanthes minutissima" ~ "achnanthidium minutissimum",
      latin == "nuria danrica" ~ "esomus danrica",
      latin == "oreochromis mossambicus x urolepis" ~ "oreochromis mossambicus",
      latin == "oreochromis mossambicus x niloticus" ~ "oreochromis mossambicus",
      latin == "enteromorpha intestinalis" ~ "ulva intestinalis",
      TRUE ~ latin
    ),
    genus = str_extract(latin, "^[a-z]+")
  ) %>%
  distinct()
```

## 1.2 Assign broad taxonomic groups
Species are grouped into three broad taxonomic domains: algae, invertebrates, and fish.
```{r}
algae_phyla <- c(
  "chlorophyta", "charophyta", "rhodophyta", "ochrophyta",
  "haptophyta", "cryptophyta", "cyanobacteria", "myzozoa", "euglenozoa"
)

fish_classes <- c(
  "actinopterygii", "petromyzonti", "elasmobranchii",
  "chondrichthyes", "myxini", "hyperoartia", "sarcopterygii"
)

spe_tax_clean <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      phylum %in% algae_phyla ~ "algae",
      class %in% fish_classes ~ "fish",
      kingdom == "animalia" ~ "invertebrate",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Inspect unclassified records before removing them
spe_tax_clean %>%
  filter(is.na(group)) %>%
  count(kingdom, phylum, class, sort = TRUE) %>%
  kable()

spe_tax_clean <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(group))

tax_summary_clean <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_species = n_distinct(latin),
    n_genus = n_distinct(genus),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(tax_summary_clean)
```


# 2. Build genus level phylogenies

We build a genus level phylogeny tree using the Open Tree of Life. We standardize
branch lengths using Grafen’s method and filter our dataset to only
species present in the tree. In the end of this script, we further prine thr tree to algae tree, invertebrate tree and vertebrate tree.

At the end of this section, the taxonomy dataset is filtered to retain only
species whose genus is present in the full genus-level phylogeny.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
match_genus_group_tx <- function(df_group,
                                 context_name = "All life",
                                 do_approximate_matching = TRUE) {
  genus_names <- df_group %>%
    pull(genus) %>%
    unique() %>%
    sort() %>%
    as.character()

  tnrs_match_names(
    names = genus_names,
    context_name = context_name,
    do_approximate_matching = do_approximate_matching
  )
}

rename_tree_tips_to_genus <- function(tree, tx_match) {
  tip_ott <- as.numeric(gsub(".*_ott", "", tree$tip.label))

  tree$tip.label <- tolower(tx_match$search_string[
    match(tip_ott, tx_match$ott_id)
  ])

  tree
}
```

## 2.1 Match genera to Open Tree Taxonomy

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
df_algae <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  filter(group == "algae")

df_inv <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  filter(group == "invertebrate")

df_fish <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  filter(group == "fish")

res_algae <- match_genus_group_tx(
  df_algae,
  context_name = "All life"
)

res_inv <- match_genus_group_tx(
  df_inv,
  context_name = "Animals"
)

res_fish <- match_genus_group_tx(
  df_fish,
  context_name = "Animals"
)
```

```{r}
ott_match_summary <- tibble(
  group = c("algae", "invertebrate", "fish"),
  n_input_genus = c(
    n_distinct(df_algae$genus),
    n_distinct(df_inv$genus),
    n_distinct(df_fish$genus)
  ),
  n_matched_ott = c(
    sum(!is.na(res_algae$ott_id)),
    sum(!is.na(res_inv$ott_id)),
    sum(!is.na(res_fish$ott_id))
  )
)

kable(ott_match_summary)
```

## 2.2 Build separate genus-level trees

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Algae tree
algae_ott_ids <- ott_id(res_algae)
algae_ott_in_tree <- algae_ott_ids[is_in_tree(algae_ott_ids)]

algae_tree <- tol_induced_subtree(ott_ids = algae_ott_in_tree)

algae_tree <- rename_tree_tips_to_genus(tree = algae_tree,
                                        tx_match = res_algae)

# Invertebrate tree
inv_ott_ids <- ott_id(res_inv)
inv_ott_in_tree <- inv_ott_ids[is_in_tree(inv_ott_ids)]

inv_tree <- tol_induced_subtree(ott_ids = inv_ott_in_tree)

inv_tree <- rename_tree_tips_to_genus(tree = inv_tree,
                                      tx_match = res_inv)

# Fish tree
fish_ott_ids <- ott_id(res_fish)
fish_ott_in_tree <- fish_ott_ids[is_in_tree(fish_ott_ids)]

fish_tree <- tol_induced_subtree(ott_ids = fish_ott_in_tree)

fish_tree <- rename_tree_tips_to_genus(tree = fish_tree, 
                                       tx_match = res_fish)
```

```{r}
separate_tree_summary <- tibble(
  group = c("algae", "invertebrate", "fish"),
  n_ott_in_tree = c(
    length(algae_ott_in_tree),
    length(inv_ott_in_tree),
    length(fish_ott_in_tree)
  ),
  n_tree_tips = c(
    length(algae_tree$tip.label),
    length(inv_tree$tip.label),
    length(fish_tree$tip.label)
  )
)

kable(separate_tree_summary)
```

## 2.3 Build the full genus-level tree

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
tx_full <- bind_rows(
  res_algae,
  res_inv,
  res_fish
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ott_id)) %>%
  distinct(ott_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

full_ott_ids <- unique(tx_full$ott_id)
full_ott_in_tree <- full_ott_ids[is_in_tree(full_ott_ids)]

full_tree <- tol_induced_subtree(ott_ids = full_ott_in_tree)

full_tree <- rename_tree_tips_to_genus(tree = full_tree, 
                                       tx_match = tx_full)
```

```{r}
full_tree_summary <- tibble(
  tree = "full",
  n_ott_ids = length(full_ott_ids),
  n_ott_in_tree = length(full_ott_in_tree),
  n_tree_tips = length(full_tree$tip.label)
)

kable(full_tree_summary)
```

## 2.4 Compare separate trees with pruned full tree

This check verifies whether pruning the full tree produces the same set of
genera as building separate taxon-specific trees directly.

```{r}
pruned_full_algae_tree <- keep.tip(
  full_tree,
  intersect(full_tree$tip.label, df_algae$genus)
)

pruned_full_inv_tree <- keep.tip(
  full_tree,
  intersect(full_tree$tip.label, df_inv$genus)
)

pruned_full_fish_tree <- keep.tip(
  full_tree,
  intersect(full_tree$tip.label, df_fish$genus)
)

tree_comparison_summary <- tibble(
  group = c("algae", "invertebrate", "fish"),
  n_tips_separate_tree = c(
    length(algae_tree$tip.label),
    length(inv_tree$tip.label),
    length(fish_tree$tip.label)
  ),
  n_tips_pruned_full_tree = c(
    length(pruned_full_algae_tree$tip.label),
    length(pruned_full_inv_tree$tip.label),
    length(pruned_full_fish_tree$tip.label)
  ),
  same_tip_set = c(
    setequal(algae_tree$tip.label, pruned_full_algae_tree$tip.label),
    setequal(inv_tree$tip.label, pruned_full_inv_tree$tip.label),
    setequal(fish_tree$tip.label, pruned_full_fish_tree$tip.label)
  )
)

kable(tree_comparison_summary)
```

## 2.5 Standardise branch lengths

Because Open Tree induced subtrees do not always provide branch lengths suitable
for comparative analyses, we standardise branch lengths using Grafen's method.

```{r}
algae_tree_raw <- compute.brlen(
  algae_tree,
  method = "Grafen"
)

inv_tree_raw <- compute.brlen(
  inv_tree,
  method = "Grafen"
)

fish_tree_raw <- compute.brlen(
  fish_tree,
  method = "Grafen"
)

full_tree_raw <- compute.brlen(
  full_tree,
  method = "Grafen"
)
```

```{r}
branch_length_summary <- tibble(
  tree = c("algae", "invertebrate", "fish", "full"),
  n_tips = c(
    length(algae_tree_raw$tip.label),
    length(inv_tree_raw$tip.label),
    length(fish_tree_raw$tip.label),
    length(full_tree_raw$tip.label)
  ),
  has_branch_lengths = c(
    !is.null(algae_tree_raw$edge.length),
    !is.null(inv_tree_raw$edge.length),
    !is.null(fish_tree_raw$edge.length),
    !is.null(full_tree_raw$edge.length)
  )
)

kable(branch_length_summary)
```

## 2.6 Filter taxonomy to genera present in the phylogeny

```{r}
genus_in_tree <- full_tree_raw$tip.label

spe_tax_clean_tree <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  filter(genus %in% genus_in_tree)

tree_filtered_tax_summary <- spe_tax_clean_tree %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_species = n_distinct(latin),
    n_genus = n_distinct(genus),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(tree_filtered_tax_summary)
```

# 3. Assemble body masses

We add each species with body mass estimates from a curated literature
database. The matching proceeds in two steps:

-   Species level: exact match on species name.

-   Genus level fallback: if species data are missing, we assign the
    genus average.

```{r}
sp_BM <- readRDS(here("data/4_body_mass/BM_species_summary.rds")) %>%
  mutate(
    latin = tolower(latin),
    genus = tolower(genus)
  ) %>%
  rename(BMsource = sources)

tomatch_BM <- spe_tax_clean_tree %>% select(latin, genus)

# Species-level match
species_match <- tomatch_BM %>%
  left_join(sp_BM %>% select(latin, mean_mass_g, BMsource), by = "latin") %>%
  mutate(BM_match_level = ifelse(!is.na(mean_mass_g), "species", NA))

n_species_match <- n_distinct(species_match$latin[species_match$BM_match_level == "species"])
n_species_match

# Genus-level fallback for unmatched species
# Compute genus average mass from sp_BM
genus_avg <- sp_BM %>%
  group_by(genus) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_mass_g_genus = mean(mean_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE),
    BMsource = paste(unique(BMsource), collapse = "; "), 
    .groups = "drop"
  )

genus_match <- species_match %>%
  filter(is.na(mean_mass_g)) %>%     
  select(-BMsource) %>%
  left_join(genus_avg, by = "genus") %>%
  mutate(
    mean_mass_g = mean_mass_g_genus,
    BM_match_level = ifelse(!is.na(mean_mass_g_genus), "genus", "unmatched")
  ) %>%
  select(-mean_mass_g_genus)
n_genus_match <- n_distinct(genus_match$latin[genus_match$BM_match_level == "genus"])
n_genus_match

final_match <- bind_rows(
  species_match %>% filter(BM_match_level == "species"),
  genus_match
) %>%
  distinct(latin, .keep_all = TRUE)

match_summary <- tibble(
  total_species = length(unique(tomatch_BM$latin)),
  species_level = n_species_match,
  genus_level   = n_genus_match,
  unmatched     = length(unique(tomatch_BM$latin)) - n_species_match - n_genus_match
)

kable(match_summary)

```

After screen checking, correct species with known body mass errors
```{r}
spe_mass <- final_match %>%
  filter(BM_match_level != "unmatched") 

spe_mass <- spe_mass %>%
  mutate(
    mean_mass_g = case_when(
      str_to_lower(latin) == "nitzschia closterium"      ~ 1.58e-09, #use genus level mass
      str_to_lower(latin) == "neanthes arenaceodentata"   ~ 0.0147, #DOI: 10.1002/tox.1021
      str_to_lower(latin) == "lysmata seticaudata"       ~ 0.77, #https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00404744
      str_to_lower(latin) == "odontesthes argentinensis"  ~ 92.5, #  10.3856/vol48-issue3-fulltext-2371
      str_to_lower(latin) %in% c("oryzias melastigma",
                                 "oryzias dancena",
                                 "oryzias sinensis")      ~ 1.73, # https://doi.org/10.1007/s10695-025-01548-1
      str_to_lower(latin) == "pagrus major"               ~ 104.9, #34, Bull. Eur. Ass. Fish Pathol., 32(1) 2012
      TRUE ~ mean_mass_g
    ),
    log_mass = log10(mean_mass_g)
  )

# Remove Ulva species with weird large body mass
spe_mass <- spe_mass |> filter(!grepl("ulva", latin)) # exclude 2 species

```

Summary:
```{r}
spe_tax_clean_tree_mass <- spe_tax_clean_tree %>%
  left_join(
    spe_mass %>%
      select(latin, mean_mass_g, BMsource, BM_match_level, log_mass),
    by = "latin"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(log_mass))

mass_summary <- spe_tax_clean_tree_mass %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_species = n_distinct(latin),
    n_genus = n_distinct(genus),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(mass_summary)
```

# 4. Assign functional groups

We classify species into ecological functional groups:

-   Algae → resource groups (Cyanobacteria, Diatoms, Green algae, and other algae)

-   Invertebrates → functional feeding groups (Filterer, Shredder,
    Gatherer, Herbivore, Predator)

-   Fish → trophic guilds (Herbivore, Detritivore, Planktivore, Invertivore, Omnivore, Piscivore)

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
algae_FG <- read_csv(here("data/5_FFG/algae_FG_alina.csv")) %>%
  mutate(FG_source = "Alina")

invert_fish_FG <- read_csv(here("data/5_FFG/invert_vert_FG.csv")) %>%
  mutate(algae.tax.group = NA_character_)

FG_temp <- bind_rows(algae_FG, invert_fish_FG)

spe_tax_clean_tree_mass_FFG <- left_join(spe_tax_clean_tree_mass, FG_temp, by = "latin") %>%
  filter(! is.na(FG)) %>%
  filter(FG != "Unknown") 

```

Algae fine-scale functional groups are merged into broader categories to address limited sample sizes. 
We exclude group Parasitic as just 1 species.
For vertebrate, we combine Detritivore / Herbivore as one group.
```{r}
spe_tax_clean_tree_mass_FFG$algae.group.2 <- dplyr::recode(spe_tax_clean_tree_mass_FFG$algae.tax.group,
  "Blue-green"      = "Cyanobacteria",
  "Green"           = "Green algae",
  "Charophytes"     = "Green algae",
  "Euglenoids"      = "Green algae",
  "Diatoms"         = "Diatom",
  "Chrysophytes"    = "Other algae",
  "Cryptomonads"    = "Other algae",
  "Dinoflagellates" = "Other algae",
  "Haptophytes"     = "Other algae",
  "Stramenopiles"   = "Other algae"
)

spe_tax_clean_tree_mass_FFG <- spe_tax_clean_tree_mass_FFG %>%
  mutate(FG2 = if_else(group == "algae", algae.group.2, FG)) %>%
  filter(FG != "Parasitic")

```


# 5. Prune phylogenies to final species set

Each tree is pruned to genera retained after taxonomy, phylogeny, body mass, and functional group filtering.
```{r}
final_genus <- spe_tax_clean_tree_mass_FFG %>%
  distinct(group, genus)

algae_tree <- keep.tip(
  algae_tree_raw,
  intersect(algae_tree_raw$tip.label, final_genus$genus[final_genus$group == "algae"])
)

inv_tree <- keep.tip(
  inv_tree_raw,
  intersect(inv_tree_raw$tip.label, final_genus$genus[final_genus$group == "invertebrate"])
)

fish_tree <- keep.tip(
  fish_tree_raw,
  intersect(fish_tree_raw$tip.label, final_genus$genus[final_genus$group == "fish"])
)

full_tree <- keep.tip(
  full_tree_raw,
  intersect(full_tree_raw$tip.label, final_genus$genus)
)

final_tree_summary <- tibble(
  group = c("algae", "invertebrate", "fish", "full"),
  n_genus_in_tree = c(
    length(algae_tree$tip.label),
    length(inv_tree$tip.label),
    length(fish_tree$tip.label),
    length(full_tree$tip.label)
  )
)

kable(final_tree_summary)
```


# 6. Save final datasets and trees
```{r}
# save the combined data for species
saveRDS(spe_tax_clean_tree_mass_FFG, file=here("data/6_combined_meta_data/spe_tax_clean_tree_mass_FFG.rds"))


# save the tree
saveRDS(algae_tree, file=here("data/6_combined_meta_data/algae_genus_tree.rds"))


saveRDS(inv_tree,   file=here("data/6_combined_meta_data/invertebrate_genus_tree.rds"))


saveRDS(fish_tree,  file=here("data/6_combined_meta_data/fish_genus_tree.rds"))


saveRDS(full_tree,  file=here("data/6_combined_meta_data/full_genus_tree.rds"))


```
